title: Truck Accident Guide for El Paso
metaDescription: El Paso truck accident guide: commercial carrier claims, 51% bar fault rules, and evidence preservation.
excerpt: Educational El Paso, TX guide — 2-year SOL, local hospitals, and insurer tactics. Not legal advice.

sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on I-95 or surface streets in El Paso can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.
Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. El Paso County dispatch will route El Paso police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: El Paso documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. El Paso insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on I-95, I-75, US-1 and in El Paso County.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: El Paso has El Paso Regional Medical Center and El Paso General Hospital among its major facilities. Level I trauma care is available at El Paso Level I Trauma Center.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: Texas reporting rules
paragraphs: Texas requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 30/60/25.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://www.txdot.gov/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Texas uses 51% bar comparative negligence; anything you say can affect fault allocation.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in El Paso
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near El Paso downtown interchange is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

sections.heading: When to explore attorney matching
paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.

faq.question: What is the statute of limitations in Texas?
faq.answer: Most injury claims face a 2-year deadline, but exceptions apply. Verify your dates with counsel.
